text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co. acknowledged the Justice Department is considering indictments against it and two executives in a federal price-fixing probe.
The disclosure, the first time the company has formally acknowledged that indictments were possible, was made in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"The company and two of its executive officers, Michael Andreas and Terrance Wilson, have been informed that they are targets of the lysine investigation and indictments are being considered against them," ADM said in the filing, a final proxy statement filed ahead of the company's Oct. 17 annual meeting.
Michael Andreas, vice chairman of ADM, is also the son of ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas. Wilson is a group vice president in charge of corn refining.

As previously reported, the Justice Department is said to be pressing ADM to enter pleas to charges of fixing prices for lysine, a feed additive, as well as citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup, other food additives.
If plea agreements cannot be reached, the company and the executives are expected to be indicted, a source close to the probe has said.
Charges had been expected to be filed earlier this week, but may be delayed until at least next week.

In its proxy statement, ADM said a grand jury in Chicago has been convened to look into price-fixing charges in the lysine market, another grand jury in Atlanta is investigating high-fructose corn syrup and a third in San Francisco is probing citric acid.
Last month, the Justice Department said two Japanese companies and a U.S. unit of a South Korean company admitted conspiring to fix prices in the worldwide lysine market.
